name: Yvette Allard
life: “I still remember forgetting the onions while covering the early kitchen.” On Monday, near Juniper Street, Yvette knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I worked the parent's late shift and nearly burned the onions. Next time I want to see the show myself.
appearance: Yvette has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Look for a blunt cut just below the ears. Away from the heat of the kitchen, the familiar outfit is a cream pullover with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Yvette looks down for a moment before saying something difficult.
personality: Yvette feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To see a rehearsal on the next free shift.
family: Alicia Sáenz is Yvette’s second cousin. Yvette chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Alicia brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The carer's afternoon*, Alicia says, “I offered to take Mum only if my sister finally saw a doctor.”
connections: Gale Farah. A kitchen worker who covered this time takes a seat beside the quiet listener at the next rehearsal.

reactions.response: Yvette waits for the parent to be seated before asking the cast to start.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Yvette writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.

reactions.response: Yvette lowers their own voice and asks for one thought at a time.
